newsitem.title: USA: Clinton declares major disaster in California, Idaho.
newsitem.headline: Clinton declares major disaster in California, Idaho.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Saturday declared a major disaster in California and Idaho due to severe storms, making federal aid available to help state and local recovery efforts.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with those who have lost loved ones or their homes and businesses in these terrible floods," Clinton said in a statement released during his Caribbean vacation on St. Thomas in the U.S. Virgin Islands.
Clinton's declaration makes federal funding available for areas struck by severe storms, flooding, mudslides and landslides beginning Dec. 28.
In Idaho, affected individuals and local governments in 13 counties can seek assistance. In California, people and local governments in 37 counties are eligible.

Referring to other states hit hard by recent storms, Clinton said: "The people of California, Idaho, Oregon, Nevada and Washington are showing such great strength and courage at this very difficult time."

"We are extremely proud of the thousands of volunteers and emergency workers who are making a great difference in their communities. We are continuing to monitor the conditions in these hard-hit states and resources will be made available as needed," he said.

Assistance can include disaster housing, grants, low-cost loans to cover uninsured property losses, and other programs to help individuals and business owners recover from the effects of the disaster.
Federal funding is also available to eligible local governments on a cost-sharing basis for debris removal and emergency protective measures, the White House said.
Federal Emergency Management Agency director James Witt named John Swanson of FEMA's Denver office to coordinate federal recovery operations.
The agency said damage surveys were continuing and additional assistance might be added after the assessments were completed.
